title: Anxiety vs worry: what's the difference
citation: Penninx, B. W., Pine, D. S., Holmes, E. A., & Reif, A. (2021). Anxiety disorders. Lancet (London, England), 397(10277), 914-927.
content:
Anxiety vs worry: what's the difference.

Worry is a normal part of everyday life. Most people worry before an important meeting, an exam, or a difficult conversation, and the feeling usually settles once the situation has passed. Anxiety tends to be more persistent, more difficult to control, and more likely to affect daily life. It can continue even when there is no immediate threat, making it harder to relax, concentrate, sleep, or enjoy everyday activities.

When should I get help for anxiety?

Everyone experiences anxiety from time to time, but it is worth seeking support if anxiety is becoming frequent, overwhelming, or interfering with your work, relationships, sleep, or daily activities. Effective treatments are available, including evidence-based psychological therapies, lifestyle approaches, and, for some people, medication. Many people find that anxiety improves significantly once they understand what is happening and receive the right support.
